newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, U.S. discuss human rights, E. Timor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, U.S. discuss human rights, E. Timor.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Tuesday he had discussed human rights issues and East Timor with a senior visiting U.S. State Department official.

John Shattuck, State Department assistant secretary for democracy, human rights and labour, arrived in Jakarta on Sunday, and is due to visit East Timor on Thursday and Friday before flying on to Cambodia, diplomatic sources said.
Alatas said that in his meeting with Shattuck "we have had an exchange of views in his field of human rights".
"We discussed the latest developments on East Timor and the East Timor talks (with Portugal)," the minister added. He did not elaborate.
Diplomats said Shattuck was a regular visitor to Indonesia and his current trip had been planned well in advance. He was last in Jakarta in 1995.
U.S.-sponsored talks over East Timor's future between Indonesia and Portugal, the former colonial power, have dragged on for nearly 15 years without producing an acceptable solution to either side.
Indonesia invaded the territory in December 1975 after Portugal withdrew, and annexed it as the 27th Indonesian province the following July in a move the United Nations has not recognised.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's new special representative for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker of Pakistan, is due in Jakarta on Thursday and will visit East Timor next weekend.

Alatas told Reuters he welcomed the appointment of Marker, whom he described as very experienced. The minister said Marker, a former Pakistani ambassador to the United Nations, would report back to Annan after his Indonesia visit to decide his next move on the East Timor issue.
